THE MANUFACTURING FACILITY AND REGULATED SUBSTANCES

The Huntsman Advanced Materials plant in Akron, Ohio is a specialty chemical manufacturing plant located four (4) miles south of Akron's downtown business district.  The facility is situated on a 57-acre tract of land surrounded by light industry and residences.  Of the more than 30 chemical products manufactured at the facility, 75 percent are consumed in the U.S. while the rest are sold on the international market.  The plant employs approximately 85 employees.

Products include chemicals to toughen plastics used in automobiles and fiberglass piping; chemicals to strengthen adhesives, paper and fabrics; and chemicals to manufacture automobile gaskets, sandpaper and tapes.

The plant utilizes certain chemicals as raw materials that require compliance under the EPA Risk Management Program (RMP) Rule.  These include 1,3-butadiene, a flammable under the RMP; and ammonia and acrylonitrile, which are toxics under the RMP.  The Akron plant operates as a RMP Program 3 facility.  The plant has in place a thorough, ongoing program of Process Safety Management (PSM).  This program includes procedural and engineering safeguards to prevent a release of a hazardous chemical, and to minimize the effects if a release occurs.  The facility invests in capital improvements each year for projects related to safety systems.  Engineering and operational controls are described below.

(1) Process Safety Information - process safety information includes process flow diagrams, piping and instrument diagrams, electrical input/output diagrams, fire water system piping diagrams, equipment specifications, and chemical safety data sheets.
(2) Process Hazard Analysis - process hazard analysis (PHA) and layers of protection analysis (LOPA) have been conducted for all the covered processes and are revalidated at least every five years using the hazard and operability study (HAZOP) and checklist methodologies. 
(3) Standard Operating Procedures

- written SOPs are updated as needed through the MOC process and include procedures for startup, shutdown, normal operations, and emergency response.  Operating procedures also address safe operating limits and consequences of deviations.
(4) Training - employees are trained on their job tasks, safe work practices, and emergency response actions.  Training is conducted when the employee is hired, when the employee changes jobs, and during the 3-year refresher training. 
(5) Preventive Maintenance/Mechanical Integrity - testing and inspection procedures are in place to assure the reliability of process equipment.  A computerized work order system is utilized to keep records of scheduled maintenance and equipment repairs.  Equipment is inspected and maintained on a frequency according to its service and condition. 
(6) Incident Reporting - Akron maintains electronic records of safety and environmental incidents including near misses.  Major incidents are investigated to determine the root cause and identify corrective actions to prevent a recurrence.
(7) Safe Work Permits - safe work permits are utilized for hot work, energy isolation (lockout/tagout), breaking lines, and confined space entry.
(8) Contractors - Akron pre-qualifies contractors to work at the facility and provides site-orientation and site-specific safety training for contractors working at the plant.  Contractors are required to follow Huntsman policies and procedures, and the site routinely evaluates contractor performance and adherence to its policies and procedures.
(9) Management of Change - Akron uses a computerized system for management of change.  The computerized system tracks changes from initiation through approval, and includes a mechanism for affected employees to be notified and acknowledge the change.  Changes to operating procedures, process safety information, PSSRs, and related action items resulting from the change are included in the computerized MOC folder.

FIVE-YEAR ACCIDENT HISTO

RY
The site has not had an incident involving the covered RMP chemicals that meets the RMP accident criteria in the last five years.

EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM

Akron has a written emergency response plan that is coordinated with the Summit County LEPC, the Akron Fire Department, and Summit County HazMat Squad.  New employees are trained on the plan, annual refresher training is conducted, and any revisions to the plan incorporated into the training.  Employees are also trained in accordance with 29 CFR 1910.120 HAZWOPER (24-hour initial and 8-hour annual refresher).

The following activities have been recently completed or are underway to improve safety at the Akron facility. The fire alarm system was replaced in 2025. The site has a relief valve project underway, is installing a Safety instrumented System in the RLP process and is replacing manual valves with automated valves in the Latex process.
